subsystems.name: Sensing
subsystems.role: captures the user's voice, images and surroundings in real time.

subsystems.name: Compute
subsystems.role: runs AI models on the device and decides what to send to the cloud.
parts: system-on-chip with CPU, GPU and NPU

subsystems.name: Connectivity
subsystems.role: links the wearable to a phone, Wi-Fi or cellular network for cloud AI and updates.

subsystems.name: Power
subsystems.role: supplies energy for always-ready operation and recharging.

subsystems.name: AI software stack
subsystems.role: turns raw audio and images into answers, translations and memories.

subsystems.name: Mechanical housing
subsystems.role: makes the device wearable and protects the electronics.

buildSteps.title: Define the use case and form factor
buildSteps.detail: Decide what the assistant must do hands-free — answering questions, remembering conversations, translating — and design a clip or pendant that can be worn all day.

buildSteps.title: Select or design the system-on-chip
buildSteps.detail: Choose a processor with a neural processing unit powerful enough for on-device speech and vision, while keeping power draw low enough for a small battery.

buildSteps.title: Build the AI software stack
buildSteps.detail: Train or fine-tune speech recognition, vision and language models; design the memory system that stores and retrieves personal context; implement privacy controls that decide what stays on the device.

buildSteps.title: Integrate hardware and software
buildSteps.detail: Port the models to the chip, tune them for latency and battery life, and write the firmware that manages sensors, connectivity and power states.

buildSteps.title: Prototype and test
buildSteps.detail: Build working units, test voice pickup in noisy places, camera performance in different light, battery endurance, and the accuracy and safety of AI responses.

buildSteps.title: Manufacture and assemble
buildSteps.detail: Produce circuit boards, mould the housing, assemble the camera, microphones, battery and chip, and seal the device against dust and water.

buildSteps.title: Calibrate and validate
buildSteps.detail: Calibrate microphones and camera, run automated tests, and obtain any required radio and safety certifications.

buildSteps.title: Deploy and update
buildSteps.detail: Ship the device with companion apps, then push over-the-air updates to improve models and fix issues, since the AI is the core of the product.

prerequisites.why: neural processing units in mobile chips make on-device speech and vision feasible without draining the battery.
small, high-quality sensors are needed to capture usable images and isolate the user's voice.

prerequisites.tech: Large language models and speech recognition
prerequisites.why: they provide the conversational and understanding abilities that make the assistant useful.
Bluetooth, Wi-Fi and cellular links let the device offload heavy computation to the cloud.
always-on cameras and AI are power-hungry, so battery life remains a major constraint.
users need assurance that constant audio and video capture does not leak sensitive data; running more models locally helps.

pathway.milestone: clip-on and pendant assistants that answer voice queries and capture notes, with mixed on-device and cloud processing
pathway.unlocks: hands-free access to AI in everyday situations.

pathway.milestone: on-device large language models that keep personal data local and reduce latency
pathway.unlocks: more private, responsive assistance without a constant cloud connection.

pathway.milestone: real-time multimodal understanding — combining what the device sees and hears into contextual help
pathway.unlocks: assistance for tasks like translation, navigation and object recognition.

pathway.milestone: ambient computing integrated with lightweight AR glasses and smart environments
pathway.unlocks: an assistant that fades into the background and is always available when needed.
